newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks U.N. approval of wheat sale to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: France seeks U.N. approval of wheat sale to Iraq.

text.p: France has forwarded to the United Nations the first requests for food exports to Iraq under a U.N. pact allowing Baghdad to buy food and medicine with money from oil sales, a French budget ministry official said on Tuesday.
Initial applications covered 200,000 tonnes of wheat and 3,500 tonnes of milk powder and were spread among four companies, he said. He did not name the firms involved.
The official, part of a team monitoring trade with Iraq, said U.N. approval was still needed for the deals to go ahead.
Requests do not so far include sugar, another foodstuff Iraq has been seeking since resuming limited oil exports in December.
"We have passed on requests to export 200,000 tonnes of wheat and 3,500 tonnes of powdered milk but we have not had U.N. approval yet," the French official said.
Under the U.N. accord, Iraq can sell oil worth $2 billion in renewable six-month stages, with both the oil and food shipments subject to strict U.N. supervision.
After war reparations and other costs, about half the $2 billion will be available for purchases of food and medicine.
But any contracts with commercial companies must first be passed to the U.N. via national authorities and then approved by a U.N. committee in New York.
Iraq launched a series of food tenders in December including requests to buy French wheat and sugar from France or Brazil.
Grain traders said last month that commodity firms had subsequently sold a total of 300,000 tonnes of French wheat to Iraq at prices between $195 and $200 per tonne.
Australia and Argentina were also selling wheat, they said.
Baghdad's food purchases are expected to include up to 1.2 million tonnes of wheat, 340,000 tonnes of rice and 300,000 tonnes of sugar.
Iraq will pay for the goods through a special account operated by Banque Nationale de Paris in New York.
French banking sources said the first funds were not expected to reach the account until January 13.
